1. Executive summary 
Study Helper is a calm, desktop-first AI study workspace that helps students 
read, understand, practice, and improve directly inside their own documents. A 
student can upload a PDF, image, slide deck, or note, then receive focused help 
exactly where confusion happens: on a word, sentence, passage, formula, or 
diagram. 
 
The product does not aim to become another large AI dashboard, document 
chatbot, or content feed. Its purpose is to remove friction between confusion 
and understanding while preserving the student's original course material. 
Definitions, summaries, paraphrases, explanations, quizzes, and feedback 
appear as lightweight, reversible layers connected to the original source rather 
than replacing it or pushing the student into another tab. 
 
Core promise: Study Helper keeps students in their learning flow. It provides the 
right help at the right moment without losing the source, overwhelming the 
screen, or distracting the student from the material. 
 
The strongest differentiation is an explainable learning loop: 
 
Read → clarify in context → save a doubt → answer a question → diagnose 
the weakness → practice a similar question → confirm improvement. 
 
2. The problem 
Students often work from dense PDFs, slides, screenshots, handouts, and 
images, but understanding these materials requires repeated context 

switching. They open separate search tabs, ask generic chatbots, lose their 
place in the document, save unstructured notes, and later take broad quizzes 
that show a score but do not explain the reason behind errors. 
 
The problem is not simply a lack of AI-generated summaries or flashcards. 
Many established tools already provide those functions. The unmet need is a 
focused system that keeps the original source visible, identifies why a student is 
struggling, and directs them to the next useful action.

5. Product format 
Study Helper is a responsive, full-stack web application. It is accessed 
through a browser URL like a website, but it behaves as an application: users 
can upload documents, read interactively, request AI transformations, complete

6. Approved feature specification 
6.1 Document upload and reader 
The application accepts PDF and image uploads. The document reader is clean, 
desktop-first, and intentionally low-clutter. It should place the source material 
at the center of the screen and show only contextual AI controls when needed. 
 
The reader must preserve the student's page, scroll position, and current 
selection across contextual actions. Upload processing should create reliable 
source references, including document ID, page or slide number, selected text 
range, and where appropriate, image or diagram coordinates. 
 

6.2 Contextual definition popover 
When a student selects a word or phrase, the application opens an anchored 
inline popover beside the selection. The popover should not navigate away, 
replace the document, or expand into a permanent chatbot by default.

The Doubt Notebook records moments of uncertainty without interrupting

For a selected chapter or topic, Study Helper generates five to ten source-

6.8 Error replay and follow-up question 
After a wrong answer, Study Helper generates one similar but differently

the student improves on this second attempt. 

 
This feature is essential because it changes the product from a content

The performance reviewer may mark a topic as unverified, improving, or 
mastered based on evidence from the initial answer and targeted follow-up.

8.2 Storage model 
File bytes must be stored in private object storage, such as S3-compatible 
storage. The relational database should store metadata and learning state 
rather than large file blobs.

8.3 AI design 
The model is an AI engine inside the product, not the product itself. A capable 
model such as Qwen through Alibaba Cloud should be used for document-
grounded explanation, contextual definitions, source-preserving 
transformations, structured quiz generation, and evidence-based review 
suggestions. 
 
The application should first retrieve relevant source sections and then request 
structured output from the model. The AI should not receive the entire 
document for every question. Objective MCQ grading, answer-key comparison, 
confidence priority calculation, and stable review-queue logic should be 
handled deterministically in application code. 
 
8.4 Privacy and controls 
Student documents may contain personal or institutional material. The product 
should use private storage, authorization checks, HTTPS, file validation, 
controlled upload limits, and expiring signed access links. The system should 
not expose uploaded files through public object URLs.

Document chat, summaries, flashcards, quizzes, and general AI tutoring are 
already common features in mainstream tools. Gemini Notebook promotes 
source-based answers, flashcards, quizzes, and a learning guide; ChatPDF 
promotes cited PDF chat, summaries, multi-file chats, translation, and 
flashcards; StudyFetch, Knowt, Quizlet, and Adobe each promote combinations 
of document transformation, practice, tutoring, analytics, or study materials [1]

summaries and quizzes.” Its competitive position is narrower and more 
defensible:

students understand why they are failing and shows them how to fix it

The interface must be elegant, polished, restrained, and premium in feel. It

laptop or desktop browser, including secondary-school, college, and university 
learners. The interface must remain responsive for phones and smaller screens,

5. Product format 
Study Helper is a responsive, full-stack web application. It is accessed 
through a browser URL like a website, but it behaves as an application: users 
can upload documents, read interactively, request AI transformations, complete 
quizzes, and retain progress. 
 
This should not be treated as a simple marketing website. A future product 
build should support a polished desktop workspace with a document reader at 
its center. A Progressive Web App experience may be considered later, but a 
native mobile application is not part of the current scope. 
 
6. Approved feature specification 
6.1 Document upload and reader 
The application accepts PDF and image uploads. The document reader is clean, 
desktop-first, and intentionally low-clutter. It should place the source material 
at the center of the screen and show only contextual AI controls when needed. 
 
The reader must preserve the student's page, scroll position, and current 
selection across contextual actions. Upload processing should create reliable 
source references, including document ID, page or slide number, selected text 
range, and where appropriate, image or diagram coordinates. 
 

6.2 Contextual definition popover 
When a student selects a word or phrase, the application opens an anchored 
inline popover beside the selection. The popover should not navigate away, 
replace the document, or expand into a permanent chatbot by default. 
 
The compact first view contains a contextual definition and a small action row:

technical terms.

6.3 Source-preserving summaries and paraphrases 
Students can select a passage and choose Summarize, Paraphrase, or Explain 
simply. The generated output appears beside or beneath the original passage 
as a reversible layer. It must never silently overwrite the source.

Every transformation must make three things clear: what the AI changed, 
where the original source is, and how it can be restored or verified. 
 
6.4 Doubt Notebook 
The Doubt Notebook records moments of uncertainty without interrupting 
reading. A student can save a word, line, passage, formula, or diagram together 
with its source reference and an optional note. 
 
The notebook does not become another large note-taking environment. It is a 
short, purposeful queue of unresolved learning items. Each saved doubt retains 
its original source and can later be marked as unreviewed, improving, or 
understood. 
 

6.5 AI-powered quiz generator 
For a selected chapter or topic, Study Helper generates five to ten source-
grounded multiple-choice questions. Each question must store its answer 
key, topic, expected concept, and supporting source reference when generated. 
 
Grading is deterministic. After a quiz is generated, the application compares 
student selections against stored answer keys in code; it must not make a 
further AI call merely to score an MCQ.

Before revealing a quiz result, the student selects Confident, Unsure, or

Confidence does not replace correctness. It adds important context: a correct 
guess may deserve review, while a confident but wrong answer may indicate a

6.7 Performance reviewer with error taxonomy 
After a quiz, the performance reviewer shows more than a percentage. It 
explains the reason behind each wrong answer using a defined taxonomy: 
 
Error type Meaning 
Concept gap The student does not understand the central idea being tested. 
Prerequisite gap

Each review item should display the student's answer, the correct answer, the 
expected concept, the error type, a short explanation, and the supporting 
source page. The reviewer must avoid presenting uncertain AI judgments as 
certain fact; it should allow an uncertain or needs review state when evidence 
is insufficient. 
 
6.8 Error replay and follow-up question 
After a wrong answer, Study Helper generates one similar but differently 
worded question targeting the same weakness. The product records whether 
the student improves on this second attempt. 

 
This feature is essential because it changes the product from a content 
generator into a learning loop: 
 
Diagnose → remediate → retest → observe improvement. 
 
The performance reviewer may mark a topic as unverified, improving, or 
mastered based on evidence from the initial answer and targeted follow-up. 
 
6.9 Review queue and focus mode 
The review queue is intentionally small. It surfaces only the most useful items: 
saved doubts, low-confidence answers, unresolved weak topics, and mistakes 
requiring follow-up. 
 
Focus mode hides nonessential controls and presents the source material with 
a single recommended next action. For example, after the student reads a 
difficult passage, the next action could be “Ask one question.” After an error, it 
could be “Try one similar question.” 
 
Focus mode is not an additional productivity dashboard. It is a visible 
implementation of the central product promise: fewer decisions, fewer 
distractions, and a clearer learning path.

7. Recommended learning flow 
The complete core experience should be demonstrated through one focused 
journey rather than a broad catalog of tools: 
 
1 The student uploads a PDF or image and opens it in the calm reader. 
2 The student selects an unfamiliar term and receives a contextual 
explanation without leaving the page. 
3 The student summarizes or paraphrases a difficult passage and sees the 
original remain available as a source badge. 
4 The student saves one item to the Doubt Notebook. 
5 The student requests a short topic-based quiz. 
6 Before revealing answers, the student marks their confidence. 
7 The product grades deterministically and identifies one or two 
meaningful weaknesses. 
8 The student sees the answer, expected concept, and supporting source 
page. 
9 The product delivers a similar follow-up question. 
10 The review queue records whether the concept remains unresolved or is 
improving.

not implementation 
The following technical direction documents how the product should work 
when development is later authorized. It is not a request to build any 
component now. 
 
8.1 Application architecture 
The product should be a responsive full-stack web application with a browser 
client, secure backend API, private document storage, relational learning-state 
database, and document retrieval index.

      │       ├── Quiz generation and deterministic grading 
      │       └── Review and progress logic 
      ├── Private object storage 
      │       └── Original PDF and image files 
      ├── Relational database 
      │       └── Metadata, source ranges, doubts, quizzes, answers, and progress

8.2 Storage model 
File bytes must be stored in private object storage, such as S3-compatible 
storage. The relational database should store metadata and learning state 
rather than large file blobs.

8.3 AI design 
The model is an AI engine inside the product, not the product itself. A capable 
model such as Qwen through Alibaba Cloud should be used for document-
grounded explanation, contextual definitions, source-preserving 
transformations, structured quiz generation, and evidence-based review 
suggestions. 
 
The application should first retrieve relevant source sections and then request 
structured output from the model. The AI should not receive the entire 
document for every question. Objective MCQ grading, answer-key comparison, 
confidence priority calculation, and stable review-queue logic should be 
handled deterministically in application code.

Student documents may contain personal or institutional material. The product 
should use private storage, authorization checks, HTTPS, file validation, 
controlled upload limits, and expiring signed access links. The system should 
not expose uploaded files through public object URLs.

Document chat, summaries, flashcards, quizzes, and general AI tutoring are 
already common features in mainstream tools. Gemini Notebook promotes 
source-based answers, flashcards, quizzes, and a learning guide; ChatPDF

flashcards; StudyFetch, Knowt, Quizlet, and Adobe each promote combinations 
of document transformation, practice, tutoring, analytics, or study materials [1] 
[2] [3] [4] [5] [6]. 
 
Therefore, Study Helper should not be pitched as “a tool that turns PDFs into 
summaries and quizzes.” Its competitive position is narrower and more 
defensible: 
 
Existing tools help students create study material. Study Helper helps 
students understand why they are failing and shows them how to fix it 
without leaving the source.

11. Design direction 
The interface must be elegant, polished, restrained, and premium in feel. It 
should communicate calm confidence rather than visual busyness. The reader 
must be the dominant visual element, with generous whitespace, refined 
typography, limited color accents, and compact controls that appear only when

13. Hackathon pitch statement 
Study Helper is a source-preserving AI study workspace that helps students 
understand difficult material without leaving their document. It transforms 
moments of confusion into contextual explanations, targeted practice, and 
evidence-based improvement—without the clutter of a generic AI platform. 
 
An even shorter version is: 
 
“Study Helper does not just summarize what students read. It identifies 
what they do not understand and helps them fix it in place.”

This document represents the complete approved scope at this time. It 
records the product concept, interaction model, technical direction, design 
principles, and MVP priorities. It does not authorize application development, 
source-code changes, database changes, external service setup, deployment, or 
further feature expansion.
